newsitem.title: USA: US spot resid prices resume slide on light demand.
newsitem.headline: US spot resid prices resume slide on light demand.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices resumed their recent slide Thursday as offered barrels failed to spur buying interest, market sources said.
"It's going drib-and-drab. People are looking for homes for the materials," said one East Coast resid trader.

The price skid was temporarily halted yesterday when the the benchmark West Texas Intermediate crude tumbled to its lowest price level in a more than a year on growing concerns over a flood of foreign crudes imported to the U.S.
NYMEX May crude futures today settled unchanged at $19.47 a barrel after slumping 81 cents Wednesday.
"Everyone was looking for a bounce," the trader said.
Barge traffic on the Mississippi River continued to be restricted as rushing floodwaters made navigation difficult and contributed to another in a string of barge accidents.
USG three percent sulphur material was one of the weakest domestic resid grades, market sources said.
Spot USG three percent prices finished at $13.25-13.75 with offers heard as low as $13.00. Today's quote compared with yesterday's $13.50-14.00.
Fifty thousand barrels of high sulphur, seven percent gravity material were reportedly sold today at $12.00/bbl.
USG one percent physical grade was thinly talked at $14.75-15.00, flat from Wednesday.
USG three percent paper for the balance of April held steady at $13.10-30.
In the New York harbor, one percent physical slipped to $15.25-50, dowm from Wednesday's $15.50-75. Two suppliers were heard offering supplies at $15.00.
One percent NYH paper for rest of April fell to $14.75-95, down from $15.00-10 yesterday.
NYH three percent physical widened to $13.25-75 from $13.50-75 Wednesday.

Swing gas deliveries at New York City gate for Friday edged down to $2.14-2.17 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) or $13.54 a barrel equivalent from Wednesday's $2.18-2.20 or $13.80/bbl equivalent.
Natgas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed to $1.87/mmBtu or 11.78/bbl equivalent from $1.85/mmBtu or 11.65/bbl equivalent yesterday.
